claims.text: Heated FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles undergo surface segregation before complete melting.
Surface segregation initiates and governs the progression of the phase transition.
Cu is a lower-melting-point constituent of FeNiCrCoCu that preferentially accumulates at the nanoparticle surface.
Segregation of lower-melting-point constituents locally lowers the surface melting temperature.
The starting FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are solid and compositionally homogeneous, without observable segregation.
Smaller nanoparticles have a higher surface-to-volume ratio than larger nanoparticles.
The enhanced surface-to-volume ratio of smaller nanoparticles promotes increased surface atomic diffusion during heating.
Heating-driven atomic diffusion causes progressive chemical phase separation and surface-layer formation in multicomponent alloy nanoparticles.
Surface enrichment of lower-melting-point constituents triggers surface premelting.
Surface premelting progressively propagates inward as temperature increases.
Smaller FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will begin surface premelting at a lower temperature than larger nanoparticles.
Structural disorder will appear before the particles reach complete melting.
A surface-enriched compositional gradient will be detectable before complete melting.
Increasing temperature increases lattice disorder in FeNiCrCoCu.
Particle size can be isolated as the experimental variable while composition, synthesis parameters, atmosphere, and heating rate remain constant.

contradictions.description: The experiment requires distinct nanoparticle size ranges, but the falsification design also describes the two sets as having an identical 'distribution.' If this means size distribution, it conflicts with the required size comparison; it should instead specify identical composition or compositional distribution.
